timekeeper.name: Lolo Pedring
timekeeper.prompt: Maupay nga adlaw! Mark the festival and harvest dates on our traditional Samar/Leyte calendar.

February. Note the unaspirated 'p' and tapped 'r'.
April. Stress falls on the final syllable: ab-RIL.
May. Month of the Flores de Mayo festivals in the Visayas.
June. 'H' is pronounced breathy [h], followed by 'u' and palatal 'nyo'.
August. Samar Day is celebrated on Agosto 11!
September. Marks the beloved start of the Philippine Christmas season ('-ber months')!
October. Leyte Landing Day is commemorated every Oktubre 20 in MacArthur Landing Park.
November. Spelled with 'b' in modern Waray orthography (Nobyembre).
December. Month of Misa de Gallo and Christmas festivities.
For dates & clock time, speakers use Kinatsila 'onse' (e.g. 'onse de Agosto'); for counting items, native 'napulo kag usa'!
Twelve. Spanish-derived 'dose' for dates; 'napulo kag duha' for counting.
Twenty-one. Notice Spanish loan 'uno' is paired with 'baynte' for calendar dates.
Thirty-one. Final day of January, March, May, July, August, October, December.

quiz.q: Why do Waray-Waray speakers use 'onse, dose, kinse' instead of 'napulo kag usa, napulo kag duha' when giving dates?
options: Spanish loan numbers ('Kinatsila') are conventionally used for calendar dates and clock time, while native 'Ihap' counts objects!
It depends purely on personal mood
quiz.explain: Visayan languages typically maintain this functional duality: Kinatsila for dates/time and native Ihap for physical quantities.

quiz.q: How do you ask 'What is today's date?' in Waray-Waray?
quiz.explain: 'Ika-pira hit bulan yana?' means 'What date of the month is it today?'

quiz.q: Which prefix turns a number into an ordinal date in Waray (e.g. '15th')?
quiz.explain: The prefix 'ika-' marks ordinal rank and dates: ika-kinse (15th), ika-duha (2nd).

quiz.q: What is the Waray name for the month of October?
quiz.explain: October is spelled 'Oktubre' in standard Waray orthography.

quiz.q: How is 'January 15' spoken in everyday Visayan conversation?
options: kinse de Enero (or ika-kinse hit Enero)
quiz.explain: 'kinse de Enero' is the most natural, widespread way to state January 15th.

timekeeper.name: Madame Claudine
timekeeper.prompt: Bonjour ! Set dates on the Paris calendar for national celebrations and seasonal solstices.

cards.whisper: Months are NOT capitalized in French: 'en janvier' (in January).
Pronounced with open 'ai' [mɛ], rhyming with 'café lait'.
'ill' makes the palatal glide [j]: zhoo-ee-yay. Month of Bastille Day (14 juillet).
Surprise: spelled with 4 letters but pronounced simply [u] or [ut]!
No liaison or elision with 'onze': 'le onze mai' (never 'l'onze')!
The famous date: 'le quatorze juillet' (Fête nationale).
The final 'gt' is silent standalone ([vɛ̃]), but links as [t] in 21–29!
Uses the linker 'et': vingt ET un (21). All others use hyphens (vingt-deux).

earGym.prompt: Listen to the date. Which French national holiday is mentioned?

sundial.explain: The 1st of the month always uses 'le premier'.

quiz.q: How is the 1st day of the month phrased in French compared to the remaining days?
options: Only the 1st uses the ordinal 'le premier' (e.g. le premier mai); all other days use cardinal numbers (le deux mai, le trois mai)!
All days use ordinals (le premier, le deuxième, le troisième)
quiz.explain: French uniquely reserves 'premier' for day 1, using regular cardinal digits for 2–31.

quiz.q: Are month names capitalized in standard French sentences?
options: No, months are written in lowercase (e.g. en janvier, le 14 juillet)
Yes, always capitalized like in English
quiz.explain: In French, days of the week and months of the year are not capitalized.

quiz.q: How is the month name 'août' (August) pronounced?
quiz.explain: 'août' is pronounced simply as [u] or [ut].

quiz.q: How do you form 21 ('vingt et un') versus 22 ('vingt-deux')?
options: 21 uses the linker 'et' (vingt et un); 22–29 use hyphens (vingt-deux, vingt-trois)
quiz.explain: Numbers ending in 1 (21, 31, 41...) take 'et un', while others use hyphens.

quiz.q: Which preposition expresses 'in' a given month (e.g. 'in July')?
quiz.explain: 'en' is the standard temporal preposition for months: en janvier, en juillet.

Named for the goddess Maia, mother of Mercury.
Named for Juno, queen of the gods and protector of marriage.
Originally 'Quīntīlis' (5th month); renamed in honor of Julius Caesar after his calendar reform!
Originally 'Sextīlis' (6th month); renamed for Rome's first emperor Augustus.
From 'septem' (7)! Preserves its ancient place when March was Month 1.
quīnque + decem = quīndecim. Day of the Ides in March, May, July, October!

quiz.q: What were the three pivotal landmark days in the ancient Roman calendar?
options: Kalendae (1st of month), Nōnae (5th or 7th), and Īdūs (13th or 15th)
quiz.explain: Romans reckoned days backwards from the Kalends, Nones, and Ides.

quiz.q: Why were July and August originally called Quīntīlis and Sextīlis?
options: Because they were the 5th (quīntus) and 6th (sextus) months in the original 10-month calendar of Romulus!
quiz.explain: When the year started in March, July was month 5 and August was month 6.

quiz.q: How did Romans express the numbers 18 and 19?
options: Subtractively from 20: duodēvīgintī (2 from 20 = 18) and ūndēvīgintī (1 from 20 = 19)!
quiz.explain: Romans favored subtractive counting before tens (duodēvīgintī = 18).

quiz.q: Which Roman month was named for the two-faced god of gateways and beginnings?
quiz.explain: Janus had two faces looking forward into the new year and back into the past.

quiz.q: On which day did the Ides (Īdūs) fall in March, May, July, and October?
quiz.explain: In the four long months (March, May, July, October), the Ides fell on the 15th (13th in others).

quiz.q: How are compound numbers like 21 formed in German?
options: Units before tens connected by 'und': einundzwanzig (literally 'one-and-twenty')!
quiz.explain: German uses the 'units-and-tens' structure for all numbers 21–99 (einundzwanzig, zweiundzwanzig).

quiz.q: Which preposition and case ending are used when stating dates in German (e.g. 'on the 3rd of October')?
options: The dative contraction 'am' (= an dem) + ordinal suffix '-ten': am dritten Oktober!
quiz.explain: 'am' (an dem) triggers the dative case on the ordinal number: am ersten, am dritten, am zwanzigsten.

quiz.q: Why do German speakers sometimes say 'Juno' and 'Julei' on telephone or radio broadcasts?
options: To clearly distinguish 'Juni' (June) and 'Juli' (July), which sound dangerously similar over audio!
Because they are archaic dialect words
quiz.explain: Juni and Juli differ by only one consonant, so 'Juno' and 'Julei' eliminate ambiguity.

quiz.q: How does the spelling of 'dreißig' (30) differ from 'zwanzig' (20) and 'vierzig' (40)?
options: dreißig uses the Eszett 'ß', while other tens end in '-zig' with a 'z'!
quiz.explain: dreißig is unique among the tens in keeping '-ßig' instead of '-zig'.

quiz.q: How is the letter 'J' pronounced in the German months 'Januar', 'Juni', and 'Juli'?
quiz.explain: German 'J' is always pronounced like an English 'Y' [j].
